root_cause: In rich/pretty.py traverse(), the dataclass branch iterates `fields(obj) if field.repr` and calls getattr(obj, field.name). A dataclass field declared field(init=False) with no default is listed by fields() but never set on the instance, so getattr raises AttributeError and pretty printing (and pretty tracebacks) crash.
best_solution: Filter the dataclass field generator to fields that actually exist on the instance: `field for field in fields(obj) if field.repr and hasattr(obj, field.name)`. A missing field is silently skipped, so a dataclass whose only field is unset renders via the node's existing empty=`Name()` form, i.e. `BadDataclass()`. Reasoning from the statement: 'missing field in dataclass' means an attribute declared in fields() but absent on the object; the only place rich reads dataclass fields is the loop in pretty.traverse, so guard the getattr there.
acceptable_alternatives: Wrapping getattr in try/except AttributeError and skipping the field, or getattr with a sentinel default and skipping on sentinel, would also produce 'BadDataclass()\n'. Rendering a placeholder for the missing field would fail the exact-string test.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_pretty.py::test_dataclass_no_attribute: @dataclass(eq=False) class BadDataclass: item: int = field(init=False); console.print(BadDataclass()) captured must equal exactly 'BadDataclass()\n' (missing field omitted, no error, no placeholder).
locating_signals: Statement is only the PR title 'fix for missing field in dataclass' plus a bare issue URL; the function is not named. 'dataclass' + rich leads to rich/pretty.py's is_dataclass branch in traverse(), which is the only fields() loop. The linked issue text (not visible to the agent) names init=False and points at the exact getattr line.
our_outcome_summary: Failed on all four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass false). v4 (295s, 102 calls) committed only a dozen scratch repro scripts (reproduce_issue.py, test_dataclass_repr_false_*.py, test_node*.py) and no source change; it misread 'missing field' as field(repr=False). v6 added `empty=f"{obj.__class__.__name__}()"` to the dataclass Node, which already existed at base, plus attrs/repr=False repro files; the getattr still raised. v7 added an unused `is_dataclass: bool = False` field to the Node dataclass, a no-op. v8 produced an empty patch. The p_v4 test log shows the untouched line rich/pretty.py:786 raising AttributeError: 'BadDataclass' object has no attribute 'item'. Every config guessed the wrong meaning of 'missing field' (repr=False or empty rendering) instead of a declared-but-unset attribute (init=False, no default).
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is a terse title plus a bare issue link, reconstruct the failing input before editing: enumerate the concrete ways the named thing can be 'missing' (here, a dataclass field declared with init=False and no default, so fields() lists it but the instance lacks the attribute), write a 3-line repro that actually raises, and fix the exact crashing line with a hasattr/try-except guard. If a repro prints fine, the hypothesis is wrong; do not ship a patch on it. Never submit only scratch scripts: the final diff must touch library source and should not add repro files at the repo root.
